newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat ends mostly higher on soybean gains.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat ends mostly higher on soybean gains.

text.p: CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed mostly higher on gains in soybeans and on short covering tied to signals the market was oversold late Monday, traders said.
But gains were capped by signals U.S. wheat crop prospects were improving, traders said.

Early cuttings show that Oklahoma may produce a hard red winter wheat crop this year that exceeds initial expectations for quality and quantity, agronomists and grain inspectors said Tuesday. Freezing weather hit the crop in April but a cool and wet spring helped the crop rebound.
Also recent rainfall in key U.S. spring wheat producing areas limited the advances.
USDA Monday said the spring wheat crop as of Sunday was 97 percent seeded, ahead of 92 percent of a year ago and above the 96 percent average.
USDA Monday said the U.S. winter wheat crop was 61 percent good to excellent, above 60 percent in that category the previous week.
CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed 1-1/2 cents higher to one cent lower, with July up one at $3.43-3/4.

Refco Inc and Merrill Lynch Futures each bought 1.5 million bushels of July, traders said. Cargill Inc sold 1.5 million July and sold two million September, traders said. Also Term Commodities sold three million September and Prudential Securities soldtwo million bushels of September, traders said.
In spread trading, Prudential Securities did one million bushels of September/July at 8-1/2 cents, premium September, traders said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 19,000 contracts, below the 23,644 traded Monday.

In wheat options, Paine Webber bought 400 September $5.00 calls at 5/8 cent, LFG Futures bought 300 July $3.70 puts at 27 to 27-1/4 cents and Smith Barney sold 175 July $3.50 puts at nine cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 7,000 contracts, below the 10,340 traded Monday.
